23001.desc:
Check your Commander Level by tapping your profile icon on the top-left side of the home screen.
You can gain EXP towards your Commander Level every time you sortie. After accumulating enough Commander EXP, your Commander Level will increase.
23001.name: Reach Commander Level 5.

23002.desc:
Raising your Commander Level has the following benefits:
- Unlocks certain game features and stages
- Increases your Oil and Coin stockpile limits
- Increases the number of commissions that appear, and increases the number of commissions you can send at once
- Unlocks Daily Challenge stages
- Increases the rate at which the dorms generate EXP
- Increases the upgrade level cap for facilities such as the Canteen and Merchant.
23002.name: Reach Commander Level 10.

23003.desc:
From the home screen, tap the "Build" button to head to the construction page. On the construction page, you can check all currently ongoing orders from the limited-time and permanent pools. The "Light", "Heavy", and "Special" pools are considered permanent pools.
Wisdom Cubes and Coins are required for each construction attempt. When carrying out construction, shipgirls will appear at set probability rates. When building from the Heavy and Special permanent pools, you will have a chance to obtain UR-rarity ships.
When building from a Limited Construction pool, you will be able to obtain the shipgirls that appear during that event period.
The shipgirls that appear in the permanent pools are subject to change.
23003.name: Build 1 ship.

23004.desc:
From the home screen, tap the "Build" button to head to the construction page. On the construction page, you can view the time for ships currently under construction, and instantly complete this process by using a Quick Finisher.
Each shipgirl takes a certain amount of time to finish building, and each shipgirl has her own corresponding build time.
Only 2 shipgirls can be under construction at the same time.
By tapping the "Finish All" button, you will be able to consume Quick Finishers to instantly complete all ships currently under construction.
By toggling the "Automatically lock new characters" option to ON from the bottom-right of the screen, you can automatically lock the first copy of each unique shipgirl you obtain.
23004.name: Use 1 Quick Finisher.

23005.desc:
From the home screen, tap the "Build" button to head to the construction page. From the "Requisition" page, you will be able to spend Medals of Honor to call for shipgirls to assist you.
Medals of Honor can be obtained from retiring shipgirls.
Shipgirls obtained through requisition do not take time to build, and will be obtained immediately.
23005.name: Perform requisition 1 time.

23006.desc:
From the home screen, tap the "Build" button to head to the construction page. You can see which UR shipgirls are available for exchange by tapping the "View Choice" button on the right side of the screen.
Each time you build a ship in a permanent construction pool or some limited construction pools, you will obtain Permanent UR Exchange points equal to the number of cubes spent. You will also be able to obtain these points by spending Build Tickets, which are available from certain events.
Upon reaching 400 Permanent UR Exchange points, you can spend them all to obtain one of the featured UR ships of your choosing.
23006.name: Exchange for 1 permanent UR ship.

23007.desc:
From the home screen, tap the "Build" button to head to the construction page. Tap the "Retire" button to select the ships you would like to permanently retire from your fleet.
You will receive a certain amount of resources back upon retiring a shipgirl depending on her hull type, as well as a number of Medals of Honor depending on her rarity.
When retiring a shipgirl, you can choose to either scrap all gear she has equipped, or move it to your depot.
23007.name: Retire 1 ship.

23008.desc:
From the home screen, tap the "Formation" button to assemble your fleet. On the formation screen, you will see 6 squares. The row of 3 squares in the front is the "Vanguard Fleet".
During battle, you will directly control the Vanguard fleet to move, attack, and evade.
If all ships in your Vanguard fleet are unable to continue battle, the battle will be considered lost. (This does not apply to Exercise battles.)
23008.name: Assemble a fleet with 3 Vanguard ships.

23009.desc:
The Vanguard fleet consists of up to 3 ships, with the following positions starting from the leftmost square: front, center, and rear.
Shipgirls placed in the front and rear positions are more likely to take damage in battle.
The following ship hull types can be added to the Vanguard fleet: DD, CL, CA, CB, AE, DDG (Vanguard), etc.
23009.name: Assemble a fleet with the Vanguard consisting of a DD, a CL, and a CA.

23010.desc:
From the home screen, tap the "Formation" button to assemble your fleet. The row of 3 squares in the back is the "Main Fleet".
During battle, you will not be able to directly move ships in the Main Fleet.
If the flagship of the Main Fleet becomes unable to continue battle, the battle will be considered lost. (This does not apply to Exercise battles.)
23010.name: Assemble a fleet with 3 Main Fleet ships.

23011.desc:
The Main Fleet consists of up to 3 ships, and the shipgirl in the center spot is considered the Flagship (indicated by a golden flag icon).
The flagship will gain more base EXP from battle than shipgirls in other slots.
The following ship hull types can be added to the Main Fleet: CV, CVL, BB, BC, BBV, BM, AR, DDG (Main), etc.
23011.name: Assemble a fleet with the Main Fleet consisting of a CV, a BB, and another BB.

23012.desc:
Fleet Power is the sum of the individual Power ratings of each shipgirl in that fleet. You can see your Fleet Power on the Formation page, next to each corresponding fleet.
Stats that contribute to the Power rating include FP, TRP, AA, AVI, ACV, etc.
In certain stages, Fleet Power is a requirement to be able to sortie. The Fleet Power needed to sortie to a stage can be checked individually from the sortie menu.
23012.name: Assemble a fleet with a total power of 1,000 or more.

23013.desc: As long as you possess at least 1 SS, you will be able to assemble a Sub Fleet via the Formation interface. Sub Fleets are special forces that can only be deployed to certain stages.
23013.name: Assemble a Sub Fleet.

23014.desc:
Your Sub Fleet can provide support during sorties in the following 2 ways:
1) If you enter battle in a node that is within a Sub Fleet's effective range, you may call the Sub Fleet at the cost of consuming that fleet's Ammo and Oil. The Sub Fleet will provide support in battle based on the OXY stat.
2) Search-and-Destroy: the Sub Fleet will move around the map within its attack/support range, consuming Ammo to reduce the HP of all enemies in that node by a certain percentage.
23014.name: Sortie a Sub Fleet at least 1 time.

23015.desc:
In certain stages and gameplay modes, there will be limits or requirements on the number and types of fleets you can deploy. Therefore, it is recommended that you work on assembling multiple fleets.
From the formation screen, you can change the position of a shipgirl by dragging her to a different square. To recall a shipgirl from the fleet, drag her outside of the areas covered by the fleet formation tiles. You can view the details of a shipgirl by long pressing and releasing.
23015.name: Assemble a second Surface Fleet.

23016.desc:
You can check your current progress in the Main Campaign from the home screen by selecting "Battle", then "Main Campaign".
Sortieing to Main Campaign stages may reward you with shipgirl drops, gear boxes, blueprints, and coins. You will also be able to earn Ship and Commander EXP from sorties.
23016.name: Defeat the boss of Main Campaign stage 1-1.

23017.desc:
Sortie to a stage and defeat the enemy's boss fleet to advance the progress of that stage. Upon reaching 100% threat elimination, the stage will be considered cleared and you will be able to proceed to the next stage.
You can additionally check the Threat Level Evaluation of each stage as a banner underneath the stage's icon. Upon reaching 100% completion, Clearing Mode will be enabled, and you will be able to further reduce the Threat Level Evaluation.
23017.name: Clear stage 1-2 of the Main Campaign with 100% Threat Elimination.

23018.desc:
You can check the Threat Level of a stage on the sortie details screen as a banner underneath the stage's icon.
Threat Level Evaluation:
Upon clearing a stage with 100% completion, you will be able to work on reducing that stage's Threat Level.
Lowering the Threat Level will provide a damage reduction effect for your ships that gets more effective the more the Threat Level is lowered.
Upon reaching a Threat Level of "Safe", enemies will be treated as a lower level for the purpose of calculating the effects of level differential.
23018.name: Reduce the threat level of any stage to Safe.

23019.desc:
On the sortie details screen, you will be given the option to toggle on Clearing Mode for that stage upon reaching 100% completion.
Clearing Mode:
Enemy air raids and ambushes will no longer occur, and there will no longer be any restrictions on how many tiles your fleets may move each turn.
You can additionally enable Auto-Search mode, which allows your fleets to engage enemies on their own.
An Oil consumption limit will be applied to certain stages, meaning that the amount of Oil consumed per battle cannot exceed a certain amount regardless of the cost of your fleet.
23019.name: Complete any stage 3 times in Clearing Mode.

23020.desc:
You can check your progress on a stage's objectives (represented by the 3 stars) on the sortie details screen.
Upon obtaining 3 stars for all the stages in a chapter, you will unlock that chapter's Hard Mode.
23020.name: Get 3 stars in Main Stage campaign 1-4.

23021.desc:
From the home screen, tap "Battle", then "War Archives" to view a list of all permanently-available major events.
On the War Archives screen, tap the button on the top left corner of the screen to collect up to 4 Data Keys every day (you can hold up to a maximum of 60 Data Keys).
23021.name: Obtain 1 Data Key.

23022.desc:
Each Data Key can be used to unlock a stage in the War Archives 1 time.
Data Keys are permanently consumed upon use and cannot be refunded if you retreat.
23022.name: Battle 2 times in any War Archives stage.

23023.desc:
The drops for War Archives stages are the same as the original run of the event.
Certain War Archives stages additionally have completion rewards for defeating the boss fleet a certain number of times, which can be seen on the bottom right side next to its corresponding banner.
23023.name: Battle 4 times in any War Archives stage.

23024.desc:
You can access Hard Mode stages from the home screen by tapping on "Battle", then "Main Campaign", then toggling the Normal/Hard mode button.
Hard Mode can be unlocked by obtaining 3 stars on all normal mode stages for that chapter. You may clear Hard Mode stages up to 3 times a day.
Defeating the boss fleet in a Hard Mode stage awards retrofit blueprints and Core Data.
23024.name: Clear any Hard Mode stage in the Main Campaign 1 time.

23025.desc:
In Hard Mode stages, there may be restrictions on the types of shipgirls that can be deployed in each slot, as well as fleet-specific conditions.
You will not be able to sortie to these stages unless all of these restrictions and conditions are met.
Some Hard Mode stages have a minimum Commander Level requirement as well.
23025.name: Clear Hard Mode stages in the Main Campaign 3 times.

23026.desc:
You can view the currently ongoing events from the home screen by tapping the "Events" icon.
Some events will only be available for a limited time. Participate in them to earn exclusive rewards.
23026.name: Visit the events page 1 time.

23027.desc:
From the home screen, head to "Events", then "Permanent Events" to view permanently-added mini-events.
You may only have one permanent mini-event active at any time. Complete them to earn exclusive rewards.
23027.name: Replay any permanent mini-event 1 time.

23028.desc:
You can view your shipgirls' levels by tapping on the "Dock" button from the home screen. Shipgirls will level up upon attaining a certain amount of EXP. EXP is primarily earned through the following methods:
- Add the ship to a fleet and sortie with her
- Place her in the first floor of the dorm
- Directly boost her EXP using EXP Data Packs.
(Data Packs can be used by navigating from the home screen to "Dock". Then, select the desired shipgirl and tap the "Boost EXP" button to the right of her displayed level on the Info screen.)
23028.name: Use an EXP Data Pack on any shipgirl 1 time.

23029.desc:
You can check the stats of your shipgirls by going from the home screen to "Dock", then tapping on a shipgirl to view her Info page. The stats you will see have the following effects:
HP: Determines how much damage the ship can take in battle.
FP: Increases the amount of damage the ship can deal with artillery and cannon-based attacks.
AA: Increases the amount of damage the ship can deal with Anti-Air guns.
Armor Type: Indicates the thickness of the ship's armor, which can be one of 3 types: Light, Medium, or Heavy. Each weapon has a different effectiveness against each armor type, so carefully consider the combination of ships and gear to bring to each battle to maximize your fleet's effectiveness.
TRP: Increases the amount of damage the ship can deal with torpedo attacks.
AVI: Increases the amount of damage dealt with aircraft.
RLD: Affects the reload time of some gears.
EVA: Affects the ship's chance to dodge and the likelihood of being critically hit.
ACC: Affects the ship's chance to land hits and the likelihood of dealing a critical hit.
SPD: Affects the movement speed of the fleet during combat. In certain stages, also influences the number of tiles that the fleet can move per action.
Cost: Indicates the amount of Oil consumed by the ship per battle.
ASW: Increases the amount of damage the ship can deal with Anti-Sub weapons. Also affects sonar detection range.
OXY: Affects the boat's maximum dive time. When a boat is submerged, the Oxygen gauge will be continuously depleted. When this gauge is emptied, the boat will be forced to surface.
AMO: Determines how many times a Sub Fleet can attack and/or provide support.
ASR: Influences the range that the Sub Fleet can operate in. Sub fleets can be toggled between standy and search-and-destroy mode.
In search-and-destroy mode, sub fleets will automatically seek out enemies within their attack/support range and deplete a portion of their Max HP.
LCK: A stat influenced by a shipgirl's historical record as well as the fate written in her hull. Has a subtle influence on many aspects of battle.
Morale: Reflects the willingness of a shipgirl to sortie. Shipgirls with high morale will receive bonus EXP from sorties, whereas sortieing a shipgirl with low morale will cause her to receive halved EXP, as well as causing her Affinity to decrease.
Power: A general evaluation of the shipgirl's combat readiness, based on the combined value of her gear, stats, and other factors.
23029.name: Raise any shipgirl to Level 40.

23030.desc:
To perform a limit break, navigate from the home screen to "Dock", then tap on a shipgirl to view her Info page. Next, tap on the "Limit Break" tab.
By using another copy of that shipgirl or a Bulin of the corresponding rarity, you will be able to increase her number of stars and greatly enhance her stats.
23030.name: Limit Break any shipgirl 1 time.

23031.desc:
To enhance a shipgirl, navigate from the home screen to "Dock", then tap on a shipgirl to view her Info page. Next, tap on the "Enhance" tab.
You can assign other ships as enhancement materials, increasing the base FP, TRP, AVI, and RLD stats of the selected shipgirl.
Different ships contribute different amounts of enhancement points towards the four stats listed above. Using a duplicate copy of the selected shipgirl as enhancement material will yield twice the amount of enhancement points.
23031.name: Enhance any shipgirl 1 time.

23032.desc:
Certain shipgirls can be retrofitted into a new, stronger form. Navigate from the home screen to "Dock", then to the shipgirl Info page. Shipgirls that can be retrofitted will have a "Retrofit" tab.
Retrofit nodes can be acquired by spending a certain amount of Coins and hull-specific retrofit blueprints. Certain retrofit nodes may also require a duplicate copy of the ship or a Bulin of the corresponding rarity.
Complete more retrofit nodes to increase the stats and abilities of the shipgirl, unlock new skills for her, and eventually upgrade her into a new form!
23032.name: Retrofit any shipgirl 1 time.

23033.desc:
When shipgirls reach Level 100 and max Limit Break (excluding UR and META ships), you can have them undergo Cognitive Awakening by navigating from the home screen to "Dock", then to the Info page of the selected shipgirl, then tapping the "Awakening" button that appears to the right of her level.
Awakening requires Cognitive Chips or Cognitive Arrays, and each Awakening increases the shipgirl's max level by 5.
Awakening to a level cap of 105-120 requires Coins and Cognitive Chips. Awakening to a level cap of 125 requires Cognitive Arrays.
23033.name: Awaken any shipgirl 1 time.

23034.desc:
You can check Morale by navigating from the home screen to "Dock", then to the Info page of the selected shipgirl.
You are also able to see the exact Morale value of your shipgirls when in the Formation interface or when assigning them to rest in the dorm.
The morale of your shipgirls will be depleted every time they are sortied to certain stages.
Shipgirls that are sortied with very high morale (indicated by a sparkling green smiley face) will gain Affinity, as well as +20% bonus EXP.
Shipgirls that are sortied with high morale (indicated by a green smiley face) will gain Affinity, doubled if that ship earns MVP during that battle.
Shipgirls that are sortied with neutral morale (indicated by a neutral orange face) will not have their Affinity changed.
Shipgirls that are sortied with low morale (indicated by red frowning face) will lose Affinity and gain less EXP from battle.
Assigning a shipgirl to rest in the dorm will increase the rate at which she regains morale.
23034.name: Check the Morale of any shipgirl by tapping on her status icon.

23035.desc:
You can change the secretary ship displayed on your home screen by tapping on your profile icon, then the "Secretary" button.
The shipgirl set in the leftmost slot is considered your secretary ship, and will gain Affinity over time (Affinity can only rise to a maximum of 90 this way).
When Affinity increases to 81 or higher, her Affinity status will change to "Crush".
23035.name: Increase the Affinity of any shipgirl to "Crush".

23036.desc:
As you increase your Affinity with a shipgirl, you will unlock additional voicelines corresponding to the affinity status.
Upon reaching 100 Affinity, their Affinity status will change to "Love" and you will be able to establish an Oath with them.
Establishing an Oath with a shipgirl requires a "Promise Ring", which can be obtained from Akashi's shop. Oathed shipgirls will have their max Affinity raised to 200.
Oathed shipgirls will also have their stats increased. Additionally, you will also be able to unlock special, Oath-only voicelines.
23036.name: Increase the Affinity of any shipgirl to "Love".

23037.desc:
You can view your weekly mission progress by navigating from the home screen to "Missions", then to the "Weekly" tab.
Upon completing a weekly mission, you will earn Weekly Activity Points. Weekly Activity Points are reset every Monday at midnight, along with all the weekly missions.
Some weekly missions also grant additional resource rewards such as Oil and Coins.
Accumulating Weekly Activity Points will grant rewards such as Oil, Coins, Wisdom Cubes, Quick Finishers, and Decor Tokens.
23037.name: Earn a total of 100 Weekly Mission points.

23038.desc:
<color=#e7b000>Main Menu</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Shop</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Akashi Recommends and Packs</color> sections bring you to the shop's deals. 

They feature a free weekly supplies pack, and they update with new deals from time to time.
23038.name: Collect a Free Supplies Pack from the shop.

23039.desc:
You can view the Outfit Store by navigating from the home screen to "shop", then to "Skins".
When you change a shipgirl's appearance by applying a skin, she will appear differently in the home screen and other relevant interfaces. The appearance of her chibi character in battle will also change depending on the skin.
Additionally, skins also have their own special voicelines. Certain skins also come with Live2D or Dynamic animation, and will be animated when displayed on the home screen.
23039.name: Visit the Outfit Store 1 time.

23040.desc:
<color=#e7b000>Main Menu</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Shop</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Supply</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Shop</color> brings you to a separate <color=#e7b000>supplies shop</color> which you can navigate using the tabs in the top center of the screen. Here, a random assortment of items and resources (including Wisdom Cubes and Quick Finishers) appears, which may be purchased using Coins or Gems. 

There is a chance for items in thie supply shop to be discounted. 

The supply shop resets every day at 00:00, 12:00, and 18:00 (UTC-7).
23040.name: Purchase any item from the Supply Shop 1 time.

23041.desc:
To visit the Tactical Class, start from the home screen, tap the "HQ" button, then the "Academy" button. Finally, tap the building labeled "Tactical".
You can also quick check the status of ongoing classes from the side menu. Expand the side menu by tapping the triangle button on the left side of the home screen.
In the Tactical Class, you can use Skill Books to train your shipgirls' skills.
If you use a skill book that matches the same color as the shipgirl's skill, you will earn additional EXP towards that skill.
After the class concludes, the corresponding amount of EXP will be added to that skill. Accumulate skill EXP to increase the skill's level, therefore making it more potent!
23041.name: Upgrade 1 skill in the Tactical Class.

23042.desc:
There are 3 types of skill books: Offensive (red), Defensive (blue), and Support (yellow). Skill books of higher rarity take a longer time to complete, but will grant greater EXP as well.
Some skill books can be combined into skill books of a higher rarity: T1 skill books can be combined into T2, and T2 skill books can be combined into T3.
If a class is cancelled prematurely, you will gain skill EXP proportional to the amount of time already elapsed.
23042.name: Upgrade any shipgirl's skill to Level 5 at the Tactical Class.

23043.desc:
To visit the Academy, head from the home screen to "HQ", then tap the "Academy" button. On the Academy screen, you will be able to see the level of your Canteen and Merchant facilities, as well as the resources they've currently generated.
You can also quickly collect any resources generated from the Canteen and Merchant by expanding the side menu on the home screen.
The Canteen generates Oil, and the Merchant generates Coins.
You can additionally level up these facilities after reaching a certain Commander Level using a sum of Coins, increasing their production efficiency and maximum capacity.
23043.name: Level up the Canteen or Merchant 1 time.

23044.desc:
To check the medals you've currently earned, head from the home screen to "HQ", then "Academy". From there, tap the facility labeled "Medallion".
You can change the medals you'd like to display on your profile by heading back to the home screen, tapping your profile icon, then tapping the "Style" button and navigating down to the "Medallion" tab.
You will have to satisfy a variety of unique conditions to obtain each medal, and once you've earned those medals, you will be able to obtain them from the Medal Collection Room. You can check how to obtain each medal by tapping on it.
23044.name: Obtain 1 medal in the Medal Collection Room.

23045.desc:
Some medals have several different tiers. Upon obtaining a lower-tier version of the medal, you will be presented with additional conditions to upgrade the medal.
Certain medals related to shipgirls will not have their progress affected even if you retire that shipgirl. Additionally, ships of the same name cannot contribute progress towards these medals twice.
Finally, certain commemorative medals are only available through events.
23045.name: Obtain 3 medals in the Medal Collection Room.

23046.desc:
Tap the "Cruise Missions" button on the expanded side menu to view the currently ongoing Cruise Pass.
Complete seasonal missions to earn Progress Pts. You can level up your Cruise Pass by accumulating enough Progress Pts., unlocking great rewards in the process.
23046.name: Reach Lv. 10 in Seasonal Missions.

23047.desc:
Each Cruise Pass has two reward tracks: a regular track, and a Fair Winds track. The regular reward track is available to all players and does not require you to purchase a Fair Winds Cruise Pass.
During the Cruise Pass season, you will be able to purchase certain items such as skins and gear skins from previous Cruise Pass seasons upon reaching Seasonal Cruise Pass Lv. 50.
23047.name: Reach Lv. 25 in Seasonal Missions.

23048.desc:
When claiming mail, any attached Oil and Coins are automatically sent to your Storage.
You can check your mail by going to the home screen, then tapping the envelope icon in the top right corner of the screen. You can see the status of your storage by tapping the "Storage" button on the left side of the mail interface.
Additionally, you are able to preserve important messages by tapping the "Move Mail" button to move them into the Archive.
23048.name: Claim mail 1 time.

23049.desc:
You can check your shipgirls' equipped gear by heading from the home screen to "Dock", then to the Info screen, then the "Gear" tab.
Gear is one of the important factors in determining how strong your shipgirls are in combat.
There are five main types of gear: naval guns, torpedoes, anti-air guns, aircraft, and auxiliaries. The gear that can be equipped depends on the shipgirl's type.
Additionally, different shipgirls may perform differently even when given the same pieces of gear because the efficiency of the gear in each slot is unique to each shipgirl.
23049.name: Acquire any 10 pieces of gear.

23050.desc:
You can check the gear you currently own by heading from the home screen to "Depot", then tapping the "Gear" button. The primary ways of obtaining gear are as follows:
Opening tech packs: by opening tech packs from the various factions, you will be able to obtain random pieces of gear corresponding to that faction.
Sortie to Main Campaign stages: sorties have a chance to drop gear designs, used to craft pieces of gear.
Sortie to event stages: some event maps have a chance to drop gear or gear designs.
Completing missions: certain missions may reward pieces of gear.
In addition to the above methods, you are also able to obtain gear through various shops throughout the game, the Gear Lab, and more.
23050.name: Craft any piece of gear from the depot 1 time.

23051.desc:
To enhance a piece of gear, head from the home screen to "Depot", tap the "Gear" button, then select the gear you'd like to enhance. Enhancing gear requires Coins and Parts.
Enhancing gear will increase its stats, making it more potent. Certain pieces of gear can even gain additional effects when leveled to max, such as increasing the damage dealt to Siren enemies in Operation Siren.
23051.name: Enhance any piece of gear 1 time.

23052.desc:
The higher the rarity of a piece of gear, the higher the rarity of the parts used to enhance it.
As you progress further through the Main Campaign, you will have a chance to acquire higher rarity parts as drops.
The standard enhancement cap for a piece of gear is +10, but certain pieces of gear can be increased to +13 by using Specialized Gear Upgrade Parts and Prototype Gear Upgrade Parts, found only in Operation Siren.
23052.name: Enhance any piece of gear to +8.

23053.desc:
Ships that have been Limit Broken 3 times will have their Augment Module slot unlocked.
You can view the Augment equipped to your shipgirl by heading to "Dock" from the home screen, tapping on that shipgirl, then going to the Gear tab.
You can view the Augment Modules you currently possess by heading to "Depot" from the home screen, tapping on the "Gear" button, then selecting the "Special" tab.
You can craft unique Augment Modules using special materials by heading to "Depot" from the home screen, tapping on "Craft", then going to the "Special" tab.
All PR/DR ships, UR ships, and META ships have their Augment Module slot unlocked by default. You can check the types of ships that can use an Augment Module from its details page.
23053.name: Craft any Augment Module 1 time.

23054.desc:
Augment Modules have their own mod effects. Rare Augment Modules can be uncapped to Elite rarity, then further enhanced to +10 to unlock the mod effect.
Certain shipgirls have their own unique Augment Modules, and the mod effect of these Augment Modules will be unlocked by default. By further enhancing it to +10, one of that shipgirl's skills will gain a special upgrade.
23054.name: Craft any unique Augment Module 1 time.

23055.desc:
To check the gear skins you have equipped or equip gear skins, head from the home screen to "Dock", select a shipgirl, tap the "Gear" tab, then toggle the Gear/Skin button on the bottom-right corner of the screen.
You can view all gear skins you currently own by going from the home screen to "Depot", then tapping the "Skins" tab on the left side of the screen.
During certain events, you will be able to purchase gear skin boxes from the exchange shop containing random pieces of gear skins from that event's theme.
When equipped, special visual effects will be applied to certain weapons in battle as long as the conditions are satisfied.
23055.name: Obtain any gear skin 1 time.

23056.desc:
When you acquire a new shipgirl for the first time, fully Limit Break her, or raise her level to 120, you will receive "Tech Points" corresponding to the faction to which that shipgirl belongs.
You will be able to receive additional buffs for the entire fleet after obtaining new shipgirls and when raising their level to 120.
You can check your current Tech Points as well as the buffs you're receiving from them by going from the home screen to "Lab", then "Fleet Tech".
Tap on the "Faction" button on the top right corner of the screen to see the total amount of Tech Points you've earned for each faction, the buffs you've earned, and collect level-up rewards.
The buffs gained through Fleet Technology are only applied to ships that have been fully Limit Broken.
23056.name: Reach 150 Fleet Tech Points with any faction.

23057.desc:
To visit the dorms, head from the home screen to "HQ", then select the "Dorm" button.
You can assign ships to the dorms by tapping the "Train" button on the bottom-left corner of the screen. Shipgirls can be assigned to either 1F for training, or 2F for resting.
Shipgirls assigned to the first floor of the dorm will gain EXP over time.
The amount of EXP gained is affected by certain factors such as Commander Level., effects from food, and Comfort.
The size of the first floor can be expanded with Decor Tokens, while the size of the second floor can only be expanded with Gems.
All ships assigned to the dorm will regenerate Morale at a faster rate.
Each floor of the dorm can accommodate 2 shipgirls by default. This can be expanded to a maximum of 6 slots per floor, up to a total of 12.
Random events may occur on the first floor. Tapping speech bubbles that appear will increase the Affinity of the shipgirl and grant Decor Tokens.
23057.name: Have any shipgirl train or rest in the dorms 1 time.

23058.desc:
You can purchase furniture for the dorm at the Furniture Shop. When you obtain furniture, the Comfort level of the dorm will increase (this applies even if the piece of furniture is not placed in the dorm). As Comfort level increases, shipgirls assigned to the first floor of the dorm will gain EXP at a more efficient rate.
Certain pieces of furniture have unique interactions with specific shipgirls.
23058.name: Increase the dorm's Comfort to 50.

23059.desc:
In the dorm, you'll be able to purchase snacks with either Oil or Gems. Different kinds of snacks will add a different amount of supplies to the dorm, additively increasing the amount of EXP that can be gained from training in the dorm.
As long as there are supplies remaining in the dorm, the rate at which shipgirls gain EXP will be increased.
23059.name: Resupply 10,000 snacks to the dorm.

23060.desc:
You can see which daily challenge stages you can attempt by going from the home screen to "Battle", then "Daily Raids".
When you clear any daily raid stage with an S-victory for the first time, the Quick Battle feature will be enabled, allowing you to skip the battle and claim the rewards directly.
Module Development stages are available every day of the week, but can only be attempted twice per week.
Module Development stages drop materials such as Augment Module Stones, and Augment Module cores. There is also a chance to directly receive Augment Modules as drops.
23060.name: Attempt a Module Development daily challenge stage 1 time.

23061.desc:
Supply Line Disruption stages are available every day, but can only be attempted four times per week.
Depending on the stage you select, you will be able to obtain items such as gear designs, random gear enhancement parts, and sub-related gear boxes.
In Supply Line Disruption stages, you will manually control your Sub Fleet and lead it into battle.
23061.name: Attempt a Supply Line Disruption daily challenge stage 1 time.

23062.desc:
The Escort Mission daily raid is available every Monday, Thursday, and Sunday, and can be attempted three times daily each day it is available.
These stages will drop Coins and various Parts depending on the stage you select.
Escort Mission (Firepower) yields gun, torpedo, and general parts, while Escort Mission (Air) yields aircraft, AA gun, and general parts.
The higher the difficulty of the stage, the greater the rarity of the rewards you can obtain.
To play this game mode, manually control your fleet to avoid a barrage of torpedo attacks for a certain amount of time.
23062.name: Attempt an Escort Mission daily challenge stage 1 time.

23063.desc:
The Advance Mission daily raid is available every Tuesday, Friday, and Sunday, and can be attempted three times daily each day it is available.
These stages will drop Coins and Skill Books.
In Advance Mission stages, you must control your fleet manually, either evading or defeating waves of incoming bombing ships until the time expires.
23063.name: Attempt an Advance Mission daily challenge stage 1 time.

23064.desc:
The Fierce Assault daily raid is available every Wednesday, Saturday, and Sunday, and can be attempted three times daily each day it is available.
These stages will drop tech packs, Coins, and development materials depending on the stage you select.
In Fierce Assault stages, you must lead your fleet into battle directly to take down a tough boss enemy.
23064.name: Attempt a Fierce Assault daily challenge stage 1 time.

23065.desc:
The Tactical Training daily raid is available every day and can be attempted up to three times per day.
There are three types of stages: Aviation, Shelling, and Torpedo. In each type of stage, you will deal significantly more damage to the enemy using airstrikes, shelling damage, and torpedo strikes, respectively.
23065.name: Attempt a Tactical Training daily challenge stage 1 time.

23066.desc:
<color=#e7b000>Main Menu</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Shop</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Supply</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Monthly</color> brings you to the Core Shop, which you can navigate using the <color=#e7b000>Core (Ltd.)</color> and <color=#e7b000>Core (Mo.)</color> tabs in the top center of the screen. 

You can spend Core Data to purchase items in this shop. Core Data can be earned from hard mode stages in the Campaign.

The Core (Mo.) shop is reset at midnight (UTC-7) on the 1st of every month. 

The Core (Ltd.) shop is not updated regularly, and there is a limit to how many of each item you may purchase.
23066.name: Purchase 1 item in the Core Shop (Mo.).

23067.desc:
To view the commissions you can currently undertake, head from the home screen to "Battle", then to "Commissions".
You can also quickly view the status of your commissions by opening up the side menu, found on the left-hand side of the home screen.
You will be able to send a fleet out on commission as long as you satisfy the ship and level requirements. After a certain amount of time, the commission will be completed, and you will be able to collect its rewards.
*Emergency commissions may appear as you are playing the game. There is a low chance for commissions rewarding Gems to appear.
23067.name: Complete 1 commission.

23068.desc:
The number of fleets that you can send out on commission simultaneously increases as you progress through the Main Campaign, up to a maximum of 4 fleets.
Ships sent on commissions will be labeled as "In action" in the docks, and you will not be able to send them out on sorties. If you cancel the commission, the fleet will immediately return, but you will not be refunded any supplies spent in this process.
Every day from 9 PM to 3 AM, overnight commissions that grant significant rewards will appear.
23068.name: Complete 10 commissions.

23069.desc:
From the home screen, tap on the "Guild" button to access the Guild system.
On the Guild screen, you will be able to either form your own guild, or join an existing one.
Guilds fall under one of two organizations – the Azur Lane, and the Crimson Axis. There are no differences in the features or functionalities of these organizations, so feel free to pick whichever one suits you.
Upon joining a guild, you will start out as a recruit. Once your contribution reaches 100, you will be promoted to a general member.
You can earn Guild Tokens by completing daily/weekly missions and participating in guild operations.
If you leave your guild, you will not be able to join another guild for 24 hours.
All members of the guild are able to receive perks such as increased oil storage, dock slots, and warehouse storage via the Guild Tech Facilities.
Guild members can also check the progress of these perks by tapping the "Tech" button.
Certain features of the public guild system are available to you even if you don't join any guild.
23069.name: Join a Guild.

23070.desc:
Guild members can check the progress of fleet missions, donate supplies, and collect Fleet supplies from the "Logistics" tab.
Fleet Missions: By completing the selected mission, you will be able to earn a large amount of Guild Tokens.
Provision Missions: You have a choice to donate one of three items in exchange for Guild Tokens. Each member can donate items 3 times per day.
Fleet Supply: when enabled, grants certain rewards every single day. Has a chance to reward rare items such as Gems.
23070.name: Complete 1 guild provision mission.

23071.desc:
<color=#e7b000>Main Menu</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Shop</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Supply</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Shop</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Guild tab</color> brings you to the Guild shop. 

The Guild shop is updated at midnight (UTC-7) on Monday and Friday every week.

The shop's lineup can also be manually reset using the <color=#e7b000>button in the bottom right</color> and spending 50 Guild Tokens.
23071.name: Purchase any item from the Guild Shop 1 time.

23072.desc:
Guild members can check the status of any ongoing guild operations by tapping the "Operations" button on the Guild screen.
All members must send dispatch ships to participate in guild events, and up to 4 ships can be dispatched per event.
The number and type of ships dispatched affect the speed and success rate of the guild event, and after each event ends, all members who participated in it will receive rewards that can be collected from the "Action Report" tab.
The number of dispatches is reset daily at 6:00, 12:00, 18:00, and 21:00. Each member can send 4 dispatch fleets per event.
23072.name: Participate in any Guild Operation event 1 time.

23073.desc:
During a guild operation, clear all the golden-colored operation events corresponding to the main objective to spawn the boss battle.
Strike Team: Each guild member can dispatch two ships as support to the strike team. During the boss battle, you will be able to add your fellow guild members' supporting shipgirls to your fleet. Team up and take down the enemy together!
Each guild member can attempt the boss of a guild operation once per day.
Guild operation participation rewards can be collected from the "Action Report" screen.
23073.name: Participate in the boss battle of a guild operation 1 time.

23074.desc:
Exercises are PvP battles that are carried out automatically. You can view the Exercises page by heading from the home screen to "Battle", then to "Exercises".
During an exercise battle, you will use up one of your exercise attempts to conduct a battle. All battles take place on auto battle. Quitting a battle midway will not be considered a defeat, and exercise attempts are not expended until the results of the battle have been submitted.
You will recover 5 exercise attempts every day at midnight, 12:00, and 18:00. You can have a maximum of 10 exercise attempts.
23074.name: Conduct 1 Exercise battle.

23075.desc:
An exercise battle ends when all combatants on either the attacking or defending side are unable to continue battle.
If you win, you will be rewarded with Merits based on your current rank. Even if you lose, you will still receive half the amount of Merits.
Merits can be spent by tapping on the "Supply" button on the Exercises page.
23075.name: Conduct 2 Exercise battles.

23076.desc:
Whenever you score a victory in an Exercise battle, you will gain ranking points. However, you will not lose ranking points for losses.
Furthermore, you will not lose ranking points if you are challenged by another commander and lose.
Exercise seasons last for 14 days each, and you will receive rewards for increasing your rank every season.
At the end of an Exercise season, all commanders will have their number of exercise attempts, ranks, and scores reset.
23076.name: Conduct 3 Exercise battles.

23077.desc:
Tap the "Supply" button on the Exercise screen to go to the Merit shop. Here, you will be able to spend Merits for a variety of different rewards.
The items in the Merit shop are automatically refreshed daily at midnight, but you will also be able to refresh the inventory manually using Gems.
23077.name: Purchase any item from the exercise supply shop 1 time.

23078.desc:
<color=#e7b000>Main Menu</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Shop</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Supply</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Shop</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Proto tab</color> brings you to the Prototype Core exchange shop.

<color=#e7b000>Main Menu</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Event</color> -> <color=#e7b000>Specialized Core tab to the left</color> brings you to the screen where you can see the total number of Specialized Cores you've obtained this month.

You can also quickly view how many Specialized Cores you've obtained this month through the side menu to the left on the main menu.

A maximum of 5,000 Specialized Cores may be obtained each month, and this tally is reset at midnight (UTC-7) on the 1st of every month.

Specialized Cores obtained through events, such as the Bulin Support Plan, do not count toward the monthly limit.

Specialized Cores can be purchased from the Medal shop (up to 30 each month). Specialized Cores purchased from the Medal shop also do not count toward the monthly limit.
23078.name: Obtain a total of 1,500 Specialized Cores.

23079.desc:
Specialized Cores are a special resource that can be obtained in the following ways:
- Defeating the boss fleet in Main Campaign stages, event stages, War Archives stages, or Hard Mode stages
- Retiring UR ships
- As a reward from completing certain weekly missions
- Defeating certain boss enemies in Operation Siren.
Additionally, Prototype Cores can be used to exchange for certain items from the shop.
Prototype Cores can be obtained by analyzing surplus blueprints or Combat Data Packs.
23079.name: Enter the Proto shop 1 time.

23080.desc:
You can visit the arcade to play permanently-added minigames by heading from the home screen to "HQ", then "Academy", then "Arcade".
In the arcade, you will be given a certain number of Game Credits for free every week. Spending Credits to play minigames will reward Game Tickets, which can be spent for certain skins and gear skin boxes in the Prize Shop Counter found on the bottom-left corner of the screen.
The games available at the arcade as well as the inventory of the Prize Shop Counter will be updated at irregular intervals.
23080.name: Play minigames in the Arcade and earn a total of 1200 Game Tickets.

23081.desc:
You will be able to conduct a variety of research projects to obtain rewards such as PR blueprints and retrofit blueprints at the Research Academy. Head there from the home screen by tapping on "Lab", then "Research Academy".
You can also quickly access the Research Academy from the side menu on the left-hand side of the home screen.
You can initiate a research project by selecting one of the banners, then tapping "Confirm". Make sure to check the cost of a research project before starting it. In addition, some research projects will have additional conditions that you must meet before the project can be finished.
You can cancel research projects that are not in the research queue by tapping the "Terminate" button. However, any items or resources spent to pay the research cost will not be refunded, and no new research projects will appear.
23081.name: Begin 1 research project in the Lab.

23082.desc:
After you start a research project, it must run for the specified duration before you can obtain the rewards.
Tap the "Add to Queue" button to add the research project to the research queue, allowing you to complete a number of research projects in sequence in the order in which they were added to the queue. Queued projects cannot be cancelled in any way, and up to five projects can be queued at once.
When a queued project is completed, the next project in the queue will automatically be started.
You can refresh the list of research projects by tapping the "Refresh" button at the bottom-right corner of the screen.
If a research project is currently active, you will not be able to refresh the project list until you add it to the research queue.
23082.name: Complete 1 research subject in the Lab.

23083.desc:
To access your <color=#e7b000>Research Focus</color> settings, tap on the banner on the bottom-right corner of the screen, next to the Refresh button.
By selecting a PR/DR season to focus on, you are guaranteed to receive at least 3 projects from that season every time the project list is refreshed, and a "Pick Up" label will appear on the project's banner.
23083.name: Enter the Research Focus menu 1 time.

23084.desc:
To access your Research Focus settings, tap on the banner on the bottom-right corner of the screen, next to the Refresh button.
If you select a specific PR or DR shipgirl as the target of your Research Focus, you will obtain bonus blueprints for that shipgirl each time you finish a research project.
For each PR season, you will be able to obtain 300 PR blueprints in total and 150 DR blueprints for each DR ship in this manner. The total number of blueprints you've earned in this manner for each season can be seen after selecting a season from the options on the left side of the screen.
You are able to freely choose your research focus target between different shipgirls and different PR seasons. The number of blueprints you have earned through research focus will not be reset.
23084.name: Change your Research Focus selection 1 time.

23085.desc:
You can develop and enhance blueprint ships by heading from the home screen to "Lab", then "Shipyard".
To begin development of a special blueprint shipgirl, you must fulfill the conditions displayed in the center of the screen.
Once these conditions are fulfilled, the "Develop" button will appear.
Once development has started, you will not be able to change which ship you are developing for 24 hours. Only one shipgirl can be developed at a time.
23085.name: Begin developing a blueprint shipgirl in the Shipyard.

23086.desc:
After beginning development, you will be able to start working on the development missions on the right-hand side of the screen.
While development is ongoing, one new development mission will be unlocked every 24 hours, and you will be able to obtain the blueprint shipgirl after completing all of the development missions.
You can change which blueprint shipgirl to focus on during the development process, but after doing so, you will not be able to change it again for another 24 hours.
All progress you have made towards the development missions will be kept even if you switch to developing another shipgirl.
23086.name: Complete a total of 4 development missions in the Shipyard.

23087.desc:
After obtaining a blueprint shipgirl, you will unlock the ability to Enhance her.
Enhancement can be performed from the "Enhance" tab in the Shipyard, on the left-hand side of the screen.
23087.name: Acquire any blueprint shipgirl 1 time.

23088.desc:
To enhance a blueprint ship, you will need additional blueprints corresponding to that ship. Certain blueprint shipgirls from previous seasons can be enhanced with Coins alone, even if you lack her blueprints.
Enhancing a blueprint shipgirl will increase her number of stars, improve her stats, and also unlock additional voice lines.
Blueprints can be obtained through completing research projects in the Research Academy. Setting a research focus target in the Research Academy will also allow you to earn a large number of blueprints.
23088.name: Increase the Dev. Level of any blueprint shipgirl to 10.

23089.desc:
To begin Project: Identity, head from the home screen to "HQ", then select the "Project: Identity" button.
In this training system, you can iterate and simulate the personalities of certain characters. Decide on a training regimen, set a schedule, and spend valuable time bonding in the virtual world. Your decisions will branch out into various endings.
Once you have reached an ending, you will unlock the "Special Secretary" slot in your secretary selection screen. You can view the options for this slot by tapping on your profile icon from the home screen, then tapping on the "Secretary" button.
23089.name: Start a growth activity in Project Identity: TB 1 time.

23090.desc:
Oceana has joined TB in Project: Identity, and you will be able to train her as well.
After you have finished training Oceana, you will be able to set her in the special secretary slot.
23090.name: Start a growth activity in Project Identity: Oceana 1 time.

23091.desc:
To visit the Cattery, head from the home screen to "HQ", then tap on the "Cat Lodge" button.
Tap the "Order" button to order cat boxes from Akashi Express. The first cat box you order each day is free, and up to 15 cat boxes can be purchased daily by spending Coins.
There are three rarities of cat boxes: rare, elite, and super rare. Each has a certain percentage chance to appear when ordering cat boxes.
Meowfficers of the same name have the same skill, but can learn different talents. By equipping them in the Meowfficer slot of your fleet, your whole fleet will gain certain buffs. Additional benefits may also be granted depending on the Meowfficer's skill. Meowfficers cannot be deployed to certain stages.
23091.name: Train 1 Meowfficer.

23092.desc:
When you assign a Meowfficer to a Comf-Fort, that Meowfficer will automatically gain EXP over time.
While a Meowfficer is assigned, you can periodically conduct the following three actions: Clean, Play, and Refill Food. The greater the number of Meowfficers you have assigned, the more rewards you will gain when performing these actions.
Clean: Contributes EXP towards leveling up the Comf-Fort. As the Comf-Fort grows, you'll be able to unlock additional Meowfficer slots.
Play: Contributes EXP towards leveling up the Comf-Fort, and grants additional rewards such as Cat Quick Finishers.
Refill Food: Contributes EXP towards leveling up the Comf-Fort, and boosts the EXP of all Meowfficers assigned to the Comf-Fort.
23092.name: Clean Comf-Fort 3 times.

23093.desc:
There are two slots in which Meowfficers can be added to a fleet: the Command Cat slot, and the Staff Cat slot. You cannot assign two Meowfficers of the same name at once.
Meowfficers can confer stat, skill, and talent buffs that are only active for the fleet in which they are assigned.
Meowfficers will gain EXP when sortieing with a fleet. Unneeded Meowfficers can also be used as enhancement materials to level up other Meowfficers.
23093.name: Train 3 Meowfficers.

23094.desc:
When a shipgirl has been fully limit broken and reaches at least Level 100, she will start generating proficiency upon gaining EXP from battles. Proficiency will be stocked in the Lecture Hall.
You can check the amount of proficiency stocked by heading to "HQ" from the home screen, then to tapping on the building labeled "Lecture".
Proficiency will be consumed to generate EXP Data Packs. These data packs can be collected from the side menu on the left-hand side of the home screen.
Max-level shipgirls will only generate proficiency when gaining EXP from sorties. No proficiency will be generated from gaining EXP in exercise battles.
23094.name: Accumulate a total of 10,000 Proficiency in the Lecture Hall.

23095.desc: You can level up the Lecture Hall by spending a sum of Coins, increasing the rate at which it produces EXP Data Packs, the maximum amount it can store, the maximum proficiency gain, and the ratio at which sortie EXP is converted into proficiency.
23095.name: Level up the Lecture Hall 1 time.

23096.desc:
In the Gear Lab, you are able to use development materials and design plans to convert and upgrade pieces of gear. You can access the Gear Lab by heading from the home screen to "Lab", then "Gear Lab".
Development materials and design plans are primarily obtained through Operation Siren.
Certain pieces of gear have multiple development routes. On the development screen, you can tap the "Change Plan" button to toggle the development route.
23096.name: Develop 1 piece of gear in the Gear Lab.

23097.desc:
You can view the Extreme Challenge screen by heading from the home screen to "Battle", then "Challenge Mode".
The Extreme Challenge mode features a new challenge every month, and is divided up into three difficulty levels.
Extreme Challenge battles do not consume Oil and will not affect your shipgirls' Morale, your win/loss count, and do not grant EXP of any sort.
The time limit for each difficulty stage is 10 minutes. Upon clearing a stage, your time will be recorded, and you will be awarded a portrait icon and chatbox frame.
If you already own the portrait icon or chatbox frame, it will automatically be converted into a sum of Coins.
23097.name: Attempt an Extreme Challenge on Hard difficulty 1 time.

23098.desc:
You can participate in Operation Siren by heading from the home screen to "Battle", then "Operation Siren". The following items are obtained from Operation Siren:
T4 Parts, Gear Design Plans, Gear Lab development materials, Coordinate Data for META Showdowns, cat boxes, Cubes, Coins, etc.
Battles in Operation Siren do not consume Oil, but instead require Action Points (AP). AP will regenerate over time, but can also be refilled by spending Oil.
23098.name: Complete 1 battle in any zone in Operation Siren.

23099.desc:
In Operation Siren zones, you can use various tools and functionalities found by the minimap on the right-hand side of the screen to assist you in exploration. When a shipgirl is damaged, you can either head to a friendly port to repair her, or use Repair Packs.
To navigate around the map of Operation Siren, either tap the "Overview" button on the bottom-left corner of the screen, or tap anywhere outside the bounds of the stage. On the Overview screen, you will be able to view all the zones you can currently access, and the Operation Level of your fleet (indicated by a roman numeral found next to the Power rating). It is recommended to increase your Operation Level to at least the same as the Corrosion Level of the zone you intend to explore before challenging it.
Adaptability is split up into three categories – offensive, survival, and tactical. If your allies' adaptability overwhelms that of the enemy, the enemy will be significantly weakened. You will be able to view the enemy's boosts on the combat confirmation screen before entering a battle.
You can improve your fleet's adaptability by completing investigation missions, purchasing Tuning Samples, or completing random events.
23099.name: Complete 3 battles in any zone in Operation Siren.

23100.desc:
As you secure more zones, you'll unlock additional supplies from the various port resupply shops.
In Operation Siren, there are resupply shops in the four friendly ports, and each has its own separate inventory.
When you clear Chapter 4 of Operation Siren, new products will be added to each resupply shop.
23100.name: Purchase any item from a port resupply shop in Operation Siren 1 time.

23101.desc:
A Mysterious Merchant will sometimes appear while you are exploring a zone.
You never know what wares she might have on hand, but you can be certain that she'll have great deals for you.
23101.name: Purchase any item from a Mysterious Merchant in Operation Siren 1 time.

23102.desc:
In certain zones, you may encounter Meowfficer search points. You will be able to dispatch the Meowfficers assigned to your fleet to salvage for supplies.
The resources that the Meowfficers can bring back depend on their level and rarity. While salvaging, Meowfficers are no longer able to provide their buffs for the fleet until they return.
23102.name: Salvage from a Meowfficer search point in Operation Siren 1 time.

23103.desc:
Operation Siren is completely reset at midnight on the 1st of every month. Upon reset, certain resources will automatically be converted into Supply Shop Vouchers.
When you clear Chapter 4 of Operation Siren, these vouchers can be spent by tapping the "Exchange Shop" button on the bottom-left corner of the Overview screen.
23103.name: Purchase any item from the Operation Siren exchange shop 1 time.

23104.desc:
Once you clear Chapter 1 of Operation Siren, META Showdown will be unlocked. Tap the "META Showdown" button on the bottom-right corner of the screen to head to view the META Showdown screen.
While exploring in Operation Siren, you will be able to collect META Coordinates and Dossier Coordinates. Once you have collected a certain amount of coordinates, you will be able to analyze the information to begin a META boss battle.
META Coordinates can be used to start a battle with the currently ongoing META boss, while Dossier Coordinates can be used for a selection of previous META bosses.
Upon completing a META Showdown, you will earn Synchronization Points specific to that META shipgirl. After accumulating a certain amount of Synchronization Points, you will be able to obtain that META shipgirl, as well as additional rewards.
23104.name: Collect a total of 100 META Coordinates in Operation Siren.

23105.desc:
After analyzing META Coordinates, the META Showdown will remain active for 24 hours, after which the battle will expire.
META Showdowns can be attempted repeatedly. When the boss's HP bar reaches 0 completely, victory is achieved and you will be able to collect the rewards.
23105.name: Unlock and participate in a seasonal META boss battle 1 time.

23106.desc:
You are able to provide assistance to other commanders by tapping the "Boss List" button on the bottom-left side of the screen. For your own META Showdowns, are also able to call for support from your friends as well as your guild.
When providing support in another commander's META Showdown, you will spend 1 Daily Attempt. The number of attempts is reset every day at midnight.
Providing support does not require any Oil. A maximum of 30 commanders can participate in one META Showdown.
23106.name: Provide support for another commander's META boss battle 1 time.

23107.desc:
Daily Missions in Operation Siren are unlocked after completing Chapter 4 of Operation Siren.
You can check your active missions by tapping the "Daily Missions" button on the bottom-right corner of the Overview screen.
While you are inside any Operation Siren zone, you can tap the "Information" button at the bottom of the screen to see all the missions you have accepted.
Completing missions will grant rewards such as META Coordinates and Special Item Tokens.
23107.name: Complete any daily mission in Operation Siren 1 time.

23108.desc:
You can obtain META shipgirls either by participating in Operation Siren, or by leveling up your Cruise Pass to a certain stage.
Synchronization Points collected in Operation Siren's META Showdowns are linked to the META Lab, accessible by heading from the home screen to "Lab", then selecting "META Lab". After accumulating enough Synchronization Points specific to a META shipgirl, you will be able to obtain her.
After obtaining a META shipgirl, you can further strengthen her through the functionalities of the META Lab.
If you obtain duplicate copies of a META shipgirl, that dupe will instead be converted into META Crystals for that specific shipgirl. The crystals can then be used to limit break that shipgirl in Somatic Activation.
You can level up the skills of META shipgirls either by completing Tactical Training missions, or by using META Universal Skill Books.
You can improve the FP, TRP, AVI, and RLD stats of META shipgirls by consuming materials in Rigging Fortification.
23108.name: Acquire any META shipgirl 1 time.

23109.desc:
The Private Quarters are unlocked once you've reached Commander Level 80.
Once you've entered the Private Quarters from the HQ menu, you'll be able to enter a shipgirl's room by tapping on her icon.
Once the living area is unlocked, you'll be able to move shipgirls there. You'll also be able to unlock a special 3D outfit for shipgirls who can be displayed in this manner.
In the Living Area, you'll be able to increase your Intimacy with your shipgirls by interacting wth them and playing minigames with them.
Additional content can also be unlocked by purchasing furniture and gifts.
23109.name: Enter the Private Quarters 1 time.

24176.desc:
I've heard word of an ore with the power of lightning. I'd like to test their capabilities. 
Materials required: Lightning Ore x 5
24176.name: The Lightning General

24177.desc:
So, I'm throwing a barbeque party and could use a few sardines! 
Materials required: Sardine x 3
24177.name: Lean Sardine Cuisine

24178.desc:
If Magma Powder really heats up on its own, I could use it to make the world's best fireworks! Find me one, please! 
Materials required: Magma Powder x 1
24178.name: Crackle and Pop

24179.desc:
Sparkly crystals... Pretty. Want those... 
Materials required: Small Crystals x 5
24179.name: All That Glimmers...

24180.desc:
Those plants with wing-like leaves look so pretty... Could you please gather some for my greenhouse? 
Materials required: Wing Plant x 3
24180.name: Birds of Soil

24181.desc:
Apparently, those cores are what power the Guardian... I want one to examine thoroughly. 
Materials required: Strange Energy Core x 1
24181.name: I Have the Power

24182.desc:
Bel is working on a new seafood recipe and asked me to get some shells. Don't tell her about this request, please. 
Materials required: Pourpremoule x 5
24182.name: Shelling Out

24183.desc:
Go out there and collect some of that combustible sand! What do I need it for, you wonder? You'll see~ Teehee♪ 
Materials required: Burning Sand x 3
24183.name: It's Gonna Be Lit

24184.desc:
I want one of those blood-coloured flowers for use as a hair ornament♪ 
Materials required: Blood Taun x 1
24184.name: Bloody Beautiful

24185.desc:
Those crystal ores found in the Central Foundation sound like good money, nya. Please go get some for me, nya! 
Materials required: Strange Crystal Ore x 5
24185.name: Deal Ore No Deal?

24186.desc:
Those fragments from a distant sky possess a curious power... This one seeks to learn their applications... 
Materials required: Star Fragment x 3
24186.name: Like Shooting Stars

24187.desc:
A premium fish like the Lake Master would be brilliant in a stargazy pie. Get me one, and ya can have a slice after the pie's done! 
Materials required: Lake Master x 1
24187.name: A Fishy Dish

24188.desc:
I require some Nameless Grass to use in a ninja training exercise I have planned. 
Materials required: Nameless Grass x 5
24188.name: The Grass With No Name

24189.desc:
I'll need a few of those Siren armor plates to make our training ground targets more durable. Mind getting me some? 
Materials required: Strange Armor Plate x 3
24189.name: Harder and Stronger

24190.desc:
Septrin is quite the interesting gemstone. I'd appreciate if you could bring one back the next time you venture out. 
Materials required: Septrin x 1
24190.name: Septrin for my Scepter

24191.desc:
Get me as many Spirit Bottles as you can! P.S. Teach is busy with her work, so I (Alfredo) am making this request on her behalf! 
Materials required: Spirit Bottle x 10
24191.name: Spirit Bottles, Not Bottled Spirits!

60011.name: Prerequisite for Developing Neptune

60012.desc:
<color=#a2a2a2>Enough data must be gathered to ensure a smooth development process, and the most practical and effective data comes from live combat.</color>

 — Sortie and accumulate <color=#92fc63>1,000,000</color> EXP using Royal Navy Vanguard ships.
60012.name: Combat Data Collection Ⅰ

60013.desc:
<color=#a2a2a2>Investment in engineering is essential for materialization through development. If we can apply the results of basic research to cutting-edge technology, we could make significant developmental progress. </color>

 — Complete <color=#92fc63>5</color> Research Projects in the Tech Academy.
60013.name: Theoretical Engineering Research Ⅰ

60014.desc:
<color=#a2a2a2>Through a combination of the combat data and cutting-edge theoretical engineering, development has finally advanced to the drawing board stage. However, to work out the design's finer details, thorough comparisons between it and existing blueprints must first be made.</color>

 — Gather <color=#92fc63>10</color> T2 Cruiser Retrofit Blueprints (tapping "Submit" will use up these resources.)
60014.name: Design Breakthrough Ⅰ

60015.desc:
<color=#92fc63>Combat Data Collection Ⅰ must be completed first.</color>
The first draft of the design has been complete.<color=#a2a2a2>In order to verify to what extent the design's specs can be realized, more combat data must be gathered.</color>

 — Sortie and accumulate <color=#92fc63>2,000,000</color> EXP using Royal Navy Vanguard ships.
60015.name: Combat Data Collection Ⅱ

60016.desc:
<color=#92fc63>Theoretical Engineering Research Ⅰ must be completed first.</color>
<color=#a2a2a2>Next, the basic design must be revised, improved, and optimized. This is a perfect chance to implement the ideas we weren't able to during the initial stages.</color>

 — Complete <color=#92fc63>8</color> Research Projects in the Tech Academy.
60016.name: Theoretical Engineering Research Ⅱ

60017.desc:
<color=#a2a2a2>At long last, through a combination of theoretical engineering, combat data, a solid design, and revolutionary ideas, the Priority ship's design is approaching completion. We're hoping to fix some remaining problems to achieve the best performance possible.</color>

 — Gather <color=#92fc63>5</color> T3 Cruiser Retrofit Blueprints (tapping "Submit" will use up these resources.)
60017.name: Design Breakthrough Ⅱ

60018.desc:
<color=#a2a2a2>The long and arduous design process has finally come to an end. All that remains now is the hull's construction. Oh, and the christening, of course!</color>

<color=#92fc63>Theoretical Engineering Research Ⅰ must be completed first.</color>
<color=#a2a2a2>Next, the basic design must be revised, improved, and optimized. This is a perfect chance to implement the ideas we weren't able to during the initial stages.</color>

 — Complete <color=#92fc63>12</color> Research Projects in the Tech Academy.
60426.name: Theoretical Engineering Research Ⅱ

60427.desc:
<color=#a2a2a2>At long last, through a combination of theoretical engineering, combat data, solid design, and revolutionary ideas, the Priority ship's design is approaching completion. We are hoping to fix some remaining problems to achieve the best performance possible.</color>

 — Gather <color=#92fc63>8</color> T3 Cruiser Retrofit Blueprints (tapping "Complete" will use up these resources.)
60427.name: Design Breakthrough Ⅱ

60428.desc:
<color=#a2a2a2>The long and arduous design process has finally come to an end. All that remains now is the hull's construction. Oh, and the christening, of course!</color>

 — Gather <color=#92fc63>40,000</color> Coins (tapping "Complete" will use up these resources.)
60428.name: Hull Construction Ⅰ

60429.desc:
<color=#a2a2a2>The long and arduous design process has finally come to an end. All that remains now is the hull's construction. Oh, and the christening, of course!</color>

 — Gather <color=#92fc63>10</color> Wisdom Cubes (tapping "Complete" will use up these resources.)
